To keep your Harley running smoothly and ensure it continues to provide you with the exhilarating rides you love, proper maintenance is extremely important, so we’ve put together some maintenance tips from a top motorcycle suspension company to help you out. | Change The Oil | One of the most critical aspects of motorcycle maintenance is changing the oil regularly. For Harley-Davidson owners, this is particularly important as the engine oil acts as the lifeblood of your bike. Fresh oil keeps your engine running smoothly, reduces wear and tear, and helps maintain optimal performance. Make sure to check your owner's manual for the recommended oil change intervals, but typically, changing your Harley's oil every 3,000 to 5,000 miles is a good rule of thumb. | Switch to a New Air Filter | Your Harley's air filter keeps dirt, debris, and other contaminants out of the engine. A clean air filter allows your engine to breathe easily, improving fuel efficiency and overall performance. Regularly inspect your air filter and replace it when necessary. If you frequently ride in dusty or dirty conditions, you may need to replace your air filter more often. Consider upgrading to a high-flow air filter for improved performance and longer intervals between replacements. | Tire Pressure and Tread | The tires on your Harley-Davidson are your only point of contact with the road, making them crucial for both safety and performance. Regularly check your tire pressure, as underinflated tires can lead to poor handling, reduced fuel efficiency, and increased wear. Conversely, overinflated tires can result in a harsh ride and reduced traction. Always maintain the recommended tire pressure for your specific Harley model. Additionally, inspect your tire tread regularly. Adequate tread depth is essential for proper traction, especially in wet conditions. | Change the Coolant | While not all Harley-Davidson models are liquid-cooled, those that are require proper coolant maintenance. Coolant helps regulate your engine's temperature, preventing overheating and ensuring optimal performance. Check your coolant levels regularly and top up as needed. It's also important to flush and replace your coolant according to your bike's maintenance schedule. This helps prevent corrosion and ensures your cooling system continues to function effectively. | Suspension Care for Ride Quality | Your Harley's suspension system will determine whether you have a comfortable ride and maintain proper handling. Regular inspection and maintenance of your suspension components, including shocks and fork seals, can greatly improve your riding experience.
